prompt: In a repository with an existing commit, stage only the modified file notes.txt. Return one command.
hints: Name only the file you want staged.
Use git add followed by notes.txt.

prompt: notes.txt has two independent hunks. Start interactive patch staging for that file so you can choose one hunk. Return only the command that starts the interaction.
hints: Choose patch mode.
The short patch flag is -p.

prompt: notes.txt was staged by mistake. A HEAD commit exists. Unstage that file while preserving its working-tree edits. Return one command.
hints: Change the index, not the file edits.
Use restore with --staged for this path.

prompt: After staging only one of two hunks, which single command displays the exact patch that the next ordinary commit would record?
hints: Compare the index with HEAD.
Use the staged or cached diff option.

prompt: The intended changes are already staged. Commit them with the exact message Add cafe notes. Return one command.
hints: Pass the message as one argument.
Use -m and quote the three-word message.

prompt: The latest commit is private and unpushed. A forgotten file is now staged. Replace the latest commit with the updated snapshot, keeping its message and avoiding an editor.
hints: Amend instead of making another commit.
Combine --amend and --no-edit.

prompt: Your latest private, unpushed commit has the wrong message. The index matches HEAD. Replace its message with Fix receipt total without opening an editor.
hints: Replace the last commit rather than adding one.
Use --amend with -m and the new message.

prompt: A teammate already based work on your published commit. Explain why amending that commit is disruptive, and give a better way to add a missing file.
hints: Think about commit identity and other branch histories.
A new follow-up commit preserves the published parent chain.
rubric: States that amend creates a replacement commit with a new id.
Explains that collaborators still reference the old commit, causing divergent history.
Proposes staging the missing file and making a new ordinary commit.

prompt: Create a branch named cafe-menu at current HEAD and switch to it in one command.
hints: Use a create-and-switch command.
The switch creation flag is -c.

prompt: Create a branch pointer named backup at current HEAD without switching away from your current branch.
hints: Creating a pointer need not switch branches.
Use git branch with the new name.

prompt: main already exists locally. Which command switches to main without creating a branch?
hints: Use the existing branch name.
Do not pass the create flag.

prompt: BUILD a tiny branch exercise in a disposable repository that already has a main branch and one commit. Create and switch to cafe-menu; add menu.txt containing one drink; stage and commit it; switch back to main. Show the commands, branch names, and why menu.txt is absent on main. Do not push.
hints: Keep the change on a separate branch.
Use switch -c, add, commit -m, then switch main.
rubric: Creates and switches to cafe-menu from main.
Creates menu.txt and stages and commits it on cafe-menu.
Returns to main and explains that main still points to the earlier snapshot.

prompt: Show a compact one-line commit graph across all local refs. Use log with --oneline, --graph and --all.
hints: Use the log graph view.
Combine the three flags from the prompt.

prompt: Inspect the latest commit metadata and patch together using show. Explicitly name HEAD.
hints: The object to inspect is HEAD.
Use git show followed by HEAD.

prompt: You ran git diff but want only the changes already staged for the next commit. Give the corrected command.
hints: An ordinary diff excludes the staged comparison.
Ask for the staged diff.

prompt: You are on main with a clean worktree. feature contains commits not reachable from main. Merge feature into main and require a merge commit even if fast-forwarding is possible.
hints: Choose merge, not rebase, to preserve existing commit ids.
Disable fast-forward with --no-ff.

prompt: You are on a private, unpushed feature branch with a clean worktree. Replay its unique commits on top of local main. Return one command; no interactive editing is needed.
hints: The current branch is the one to replay.
Pass main as the new base.

prompt: You have private feature commits A and B, while main gained C. Explain the graph after merging main into feature versus rebasing feature onto main. Then choose an integration strategy if A and B have already been shared. Describe how you would inspect staged content before committing a conflict resolution. No commands will be executed.
hints: Compare retaining both parent histories with replaying commits.
Merge preserves A and B; rebase replaces them with new ids. Use a staged diff to inspect a resolution.
rubric: Describes a merge commit with two parents retaining original A, B, and C.
Describes replayed A and B with new ids above C after rebase.
Prefers merging for shared commits unless collaborators explicitly coordinate a rewrite.
Uses git diff --staged or --cached to inspect staged conflict resolution.

prompt: notes.txt is tracked and has only unstaged edits; the index matches HEAD. You explicitly want to discard those edits in this disposable exercise. Restore only notes.txt from the index.
hints: The index already holds the wanted contents.
Use restore without --staged.

prompt: The latest commit is private. Undo that one commit and unstage its changes, preserving all file content as working-tree edits. Return an explicit reset mode.
hints: Move HEAD and reset the index, retaining the worktree.
Choose --mixed, not --soft or --hard.

prompt: Disposable repository: you explicitly want to discard all staged and unstaged tracked edits and match current HEAD. No untracked files need removal. git reset --soft HEAD did not discard them. Supply the correct explicit reset command.
hints: Both index and worktree must be reset.
Use --hard with current HEAD.

prompt: The most recent commit is private and unpushed. Undo exactly one commit but keep its changes staged, ready to recommit. Return an explicit reset mode.
hints: Keep the index and worktree unchanged.
Move HEAD back one commit with --soft.

prompt: Commit abc1234 is an ordinary, non-merge commit already published to teammates. With a clean worktree, create a new commit reversing it without opening an editor.
hints: Preserve published history.
Use revert with --no-edit and the given commit id.

prompt: You accidentally moved HEAD away from a useful local commit. Display the local HEAD movement history so you can find the old commit id. Do not reset anything yet.
hints: Branch log and HEAD movement history differ.
Use the reflog inspection command.
